entries.text: The dashboard answers back. The assistant now finds the lighting kit when asked about light : it had been looking for a shelf that does not exist. On Colophon, the figures row centres its last number on phones instead of leaving an empty box beside it, and the Usage link in the footer is no longer pinned under the assistant button on narrow screens. This page gained a quiet way back home, and each provider card below now links out to that service’s own usage page : Kimi, Synthetic, Z.ai, ChatGPT and Claude, so the numbers here are one tap away from the numbers there.

Softer edges on the About page. The questions section is retitled Fair Questions : the old heading claimed a volume of mail that does not exist. And the answer about shooting your project no longer leads with a door closing : the truth is a full-time job and weekends claimed by his own films, but the invitation stands. Tell him about the project anyway; help sometimes looks like advice, a lens, or a pair of hands for an afternoon.

Photos that end where the page does. The on-set portraits lose their frames : the About page's featured still (now the frame Bobby picked, warm and busy at the vanity mirror) and a new presence on the Notebook's hero : the staircase conversation from The Hook : both dissolve into the paper around them instead of sitting inside a border. The fade is drawn by the stylesheet, not baked into the file, so it melts correctly into every theme, not just the dark one.

A face for the About page. The page that says who makes all this now shows him : a framed still from the set of The Hook sits above the introduction, and below it a fold of ten behind-the-scenes frames : the same fanned, fold-open gallery the films use on the reel page, lightbox included. The photos are of the work : slate in hand, crew at their stations, the quiet moments between setups.

A podium for the top three. The model leaderboard now gives its leaders the steps they earned : first place stands taller, centre stage, in a wash of ember, flanked by second and third. The rest of the field queues below in the running order, bars intact. And the timeline below no longer indents its first lines : the invisible time stamps that caused it now live where they belong, in the hover.

Models, side by side. Tool Usage kept its per-tool breakdown : the little bars stay : and below it now stands one leaderboard that adds each model’s tokens across every tool, tagged with the provider that serves it. Kimi K3, GLM-5.2 and the rest finally appear as themselves rather than as slices of OpenClaw, Codex or Claude Code. The busiest model carries the ember bar; everyone else falls in line behind it.

The night shift clocks in. Both scenes had been empty after midnight : trees, weather and nothing alive. Golden Hour now has bats, quicker than the birds and allergic to a straight line, and one slow gliding owl : painted pale, because a dark silhouette against a night sky is simply invisible. The weather field gains a raccoon and an opossum, and the wildlife pool now follows the clock as well as the forecast : after dark the squirrels and rabbits go home, the fox works both shifts because a fox genuinely does, and rain still sends everyone off.

Colophon reads like a description, not a diary. The two sky tools now sit next to each other and say the same things in fewer words. The page explains how the site works rather than narrating what changed about it, because keeping track of what changed is what this list is for.

A footer that matches the menu. The index at the bottom of every page held fifteen links in a grid built for twelve, so three of them spilled into a column of their own and the order stopped meaning anything. It now groups the way the navigation at the top already does: Resources, Tools, Studio, and Elsewhere for the links that actually leave the site. About & Contact had been filed between Instagram and LinkedIn. Each page also marks its own footer link for screen readers, the visit counter is back on three tool pages that had lost it, and the copyright line steps aside for the assistant button instead of sitting underneath it. The usage dashboard is reached by a quiet word in the footer now, rather than an orange dot in the corner.

Golden Hour, softened. The planner’s date field, buttons, readings and light windows now carry the same gently rounded corners Drone Weather already used, so the two tools look like a pair. Its introduction no longer strands “the calculations stay in your browser” alone in a column, and the fuller note about local calculation stays under the scene where it is useful. On Colophon, the entry about the page nobody plans to visit went back to being the last one you reach.

Golden hour, weather included. Golden Hour remains the honest astronomical window, but today’s scene no longer promises visible gold through a solid cloud deck. Live cloud cover now moves both light tools from clear warmth through filtered light to an overcast grey-blue, softening the sun and moon as the sky closes. Golden Hour labels the current character of the light, shifts its color estimate and replaces flare-and-shadow advice with useful overcast guidance; Drone Weather reports cloud percentage beside the model conditions while keeping cloud cover separate from its safety verdict.

Weather after dark. Drone Weather’s original living field scene now follows Detroit’s local solar clock all the way through the day: an airy daytime wash warms toward sunset, cools through blue hour and settles into a deeper night palette across the sky, drone, tree, wind and wildlife. Its moon no longer substitutes for the sun or travels backward; it enters on its own left-to-right arc, may share the morning sky, and reflects the date’s waxing or waning crescent, quarter, gibbous, full or new phase.

Sun and moon, untangled. The Golden Hour sun now finishes its descent through the drawn horizon instead of fading and seeming to rise again. The moon follows its own left-to-right path, can share the daylight sky when the cycle calls for it, and wears the selected date’s new, crescent, quarter, gibbous or full phase with waxing or waning and illumination noted. Its arc remains a visual planning cue rather than a precise moonrise ephemeris.

Local film knowledge, connected. The LaB Assistant now knows that Scattered and Mistaken share the Detroit 48HFP Group B screening at 4:30 PM. It recognizes Mistaken as a joint ST Park Productions and Koffee Noir Productions short, can name Veda, Joe, Billy, Anton, Rylie, David, Jeremy, Brandon, Amber, Kate and Nikki as collaborators on it, and is careful not to invent individual roles that have not been recorded yet. Its notes also catch up with the current Golden Hour, Drone Weather, persistent checklist and Aspect Ratio tools instead of describing their earliest versions.

Golden Hour, framed tighter. The living sky is now a slim panoramic scene, keeping the time scrubber and all four light readings in the same view without losing the quote roller, moon, birds or wind. The selected date now settles into the open side of the hero, its introduction divides into two balanced thoughts, and the light windows rise closer to the planner. A fuller five-pine silhouette settles the right side of the frame while leaving the sun path open, and the motion remains calm when the timeline moves. The roller now travels through distinct, time-ordered filmmaking prompts from the last dark before dawn through morning gold, midday, evening gold, blue hour and late night. Colophon stories have also been pared back to the details worth keeping, with their key words carrying LaB’s ember italic accent.

Flight planning, kept close. The 18-point pre-flight checklist stays completely out of sight until requested beside the live conditions, then travels around the site until it is closed. Its higher-contrast, softly rounded field window remains movable, minimizable, browser-only and printable to PDF; it can now be resized on desktop and remembers those dimensions. Each six-item section earns its own restrained spark-and-glow celebration, and 18/18 finishes with Go fly. Drone Weather keeps its original animated ecosystem and follows the real Detroit solar clock without putting simulation controls over the scene; a faint, collapsed light preview remains for testing, and closing it returns immediately to live time. Gust-reading and night-flight notes tuck away until needed while the live thresholds remain planted in view. Golden Hour gets its own wide pixel scene with wind-driven pine tips, larger smoothly drifting birds and streaks, a true sun-to-moon handoff, and a higher, more legible quote roller with LaB’s orange italic ending.

Detroit 48HFP screenings added. The August 2 Group A and Group B premieres at the Redford Theater now carry both showtimes, one-click tickets, venue and map links; LaB’s Scattered, made as Sideways Lab, is marked for Group B at 4:30 PM. The August 16 Best Of screening and awards at the Civic Theater is listed separately, and both entries expire themselves after their screening date.

Golden Hour, rebuilt. The decorative fixed-time helper is now a real date-and-location-aware shoot planner: calculated blue and golden windows, sunrise, sunset, solar noon, elevation, direction, daylight, a scrub-able sun arc, a time-sensitive quote roller in the Story Generator style, and a copyable day plan. Drone Weather now reports actual Open-Meteo gusts, visibility and precipitation instead of estimates. Portfolio theme controls work again, lightbox keyboard focus behaves, runtime resource IDs stay unique, mobile overflow is gone, navigation and footers agree, and the public-but-tucked-away AI Usage link no longer enters the tab order. A real Chromium suite now patrols the kinds of failures static checks miss.

Maintenance pass. Story Generator tone tags no longer overwrite one another when an idea belongs to more than one mood. A 91-check CI suite now guards scripts, data, links, page structure, assistant coverage, social previews and published totals. The new tools respect reduced-motion settings, the weather scene stops drawing when it has nothing to animate, and lighter WebP hero images trim repeat page weight. The AI Usage dashboard stays public by URL but tucked behind its Easter eggs.

Housekeeping. The floating assistant was missing from Aspect Ratio, Golden Hour and Drone Weather since they shipped; all three have it now. The test that guards that had been failing on a hardcoded page count, so it never got as far as checking. Sitemap picked up the three tool pages, and the resource total was corrected to 127, having read 126 on five pages and 128 in the README since the last entry was added.

Themes renamed. Stone becomes Sepia, the warm-paper theme people actually mean by that word, and the dark weathered-wood theme that held the name becomes Timber. Saved preferences migrate automatically, so nobody flips between a light and dark page. 404 was quietly missing a theme button and now offers all five.

Drone Weather, part two. New pixel scene: wind you can actually read, gusts that arrive in bursts with real lulls instead of every two seconds, drizzle told apart from rain, and a sun that grows with the temperature. Deer, foxes, squirrels and rabbits wander through, and the drone breaks station to film them. The scene is no longer a box: its horizon is the page's own dividing line, tinted with the flight-safety state.

Flight safety, expanded. Why the gust number matters more than steady wind, what night flying actually requires, an 18-point pre-flight checklist that remembers itself in your browser, and links to the forecast services worth opening before a shoot.
Site design system unified to editorial direction. One stylesheet, one token set, one nav, one footer. Replaced 11 divergent style blocks.

The tool shelf fills out. Drone Weather rebuilt from scratch : live rain detection via Open-Meteo, FPV flight physics, flocking birds, procedural tree sway, a breathing sun and a pilot that follows the mouse. Golden Hour Helper gains interactive shooting advice with a slot-machine spin and a hero-sized sun arc. Aspect Ratio previews photos and video locally with native detection : zero upload, documented in Colophon.

Story Generator grows teeth. Fourteen genre filters, a printable field brief exporter and keyboard hotkeys. Colophon grows its tool case studies, refreshed stats counters and a two-column grid, and the unfinished ‘Still Available?’ placeholder finally leaves the portfolio and timeline.

A fifth theme, and a secret. Sepia joins the theme bar site-wide : a warm e-ink papyrus palette (shipped as Stone; renamed 1 August). And the AI Usage Dashboard launches : public by URL, but tucked behind its Easter eggs, a Konami code and a hidden dot on Colophon.

The assistant settles in. Its knowledgebase ingests the film crew, gear and production data, film queries earn video cards, and the mobile chat UI is tightened. The About page reframes itself around collaboration, with behind-the-scenes set knowledge added.

SkyBound, restructured. A Start Here path through the library, a Weather & Safety link in the hero, and headlines restyled in sky blue with orange italic. The site’s history becomes an interactive vertical production timeline with filtering and jump links.

The tools begin. The Sun Arc & Golden Hour calculator launches for filmmakers and drone pilots, the Aspect Ratio Previewer is built as its own page, the Drone Weather guide stands alone, and a live flight-safety meter joins it.
